title: Business Management Platform - Enumeration Types
description: Comprehensive enumeration types used across all data models in the platform. Version 2.0 includes global reference data for SMB onboarding optimization.

timezone.description: IANA timezone identifiers (sample - full list in implementation)

rehireEligibility.description: Whether employee is eligible for rehire

trainingType.description: Type of training or learning activity

lifeEventType.description: Qualifying life events for benefits changes

taskAssigneeType.description: Who is responsible for the task

ticketStatus.note: Uses PascalCase for backward compatibility with existing implementation

userRole.description: SUPERSEDED by baseRole + functionalRole — see docs/14-access-control.md. It mixed a platform role (super_admin), base roles, functional roles and a derived one (manager) in a single list, and had no consumer. Retained only so nothing referencing it breaks.

baseRole.description: Tenant base role. Exactly one per member, and it sets the floor. NOT a Postgres enum: roles are tenant-customizable (06-customization-model.md) and ALTER TYPE has no DROP VALUE. See docs/14-access-control.md.

functionalRole.description: Zero or more per member, added on top of the base role. Separate from base because SMB staff wear several hats — one office manager is routinely HR and IT. See docs/14-access-control.md.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes (G-10 + India + Israel)
country.note: Primary target markets for SMB platform

globalReferenceData.note: These reference data sets are stored globally (not per-tenant) and referenced by tenant databases. Organizations select from these catalogs for zero-configuration onboarding.

holidayCalendarsByYear.note: Explicit holiday dates by country for years 2026-2028. Easter-based holidays are calculated from Easter Sunday dates: 2026 (April 5), 2027 (March 28), 2028 (April 16).

jobLevels.note: Standard hierarchy used across all job titles

staff.name: Staff
staff.notes: Individual contributor leadership role (common in tech)

partner.name: Partner
partner.notes: Common in professional services (law, accounting, consulting)

timeOffTemplates.note: Statutory minimums and common practices by country for time off policies

US-PTO-STANDARD.name: US Standard PTO
US-PTO-STANDARD.description: Combined PTO (vacation + sick) - common US practice
US-PTO-STANDARD.notes: No federal mandate. 10-15 days is market standard for SMBs.

US-UNLIMITED.name: US Unlimited PTO
US-UNLIMITED.notes: No accrual tracking. Common in tech startups.

UK-STATUTORY.name: UK Statutory Annual Leave
UK-STATUTORY.notes: 28 days includes 8 bank holidays (can include or exclude)

DE-STATUTORY.name: Germany Statutory Vacation
DE-STATUTORY.notes: 20 days minimum (based on 5-day work week). 25-30 days is common.

IT-STATUTORY.name: Italy Statutory Vacation
IT-STATUTORY.notes: Minimum 4 weeks. Often varies by collective bargaining agreements.

CA-STATUTORY.name: Canada Statutory Vacation
CA-STATUTORY.notes: 2 weeks minimum. Increases to 3 weeks after 5 years in some provinces.

JP-STATUTORY.name: Japan Statutory Vacation
JP-STATUTORY.notes: 10 days after 6 months, increases with tenure up to 20 days

NL-STATUTORY.name: Netherlands Statutory Vacation
NL-STATUTORY.notes: 4x the weekly hours (20 days for 5-day week). 25 days common.

CH-STATUTORY.name: Switzerland Statutory Vacation
CH-STATUTORY.notes: 4 weeks minimum (5 for under 20). 25-26 days common.

IN-STATUTORY.name: India Statutory Leave
IN-STATUTORY.notes: Varies by state. 12-15 days typical. Plus sick leave and casual leave.

IL-STATUTORY.name: Israel Statutory Vacation
IL-STATUTORY.notes: Increases with tenure: 10 days (year 1), up to 28 days (20+ years)

US-SICK-STANDARD.name: US Sick Leave
US-SICK-STANDARD.notes: No federal mandate. Some states require sick leave.

EU-SICK-STATUTORY.name: EU Sick Leave
EU-SICK-STATUTORY.description: Statutory sick pay - doctor's note required
EU-SICK-STATUTORY.notes: Typically unlimited with medical certification. Varies by country.

payFrequencyStandards.note: Common pay frequencies and defaults by country

departmentTemplates.note: Pre-populated department suggestions based on industry

notes.usage: These enumerations should be used consistently across all modules. When adding new values, ensure backward compatibility and update this file.
notes.validation: All enum values should be validated at both API and database levels. In D1 schemas, prefer application-level validation over CHECK constraints for better flexibility.
notes.extensibility: For tenant-specific custom values, use a separate custom_fields JSONB column rather than extending these core enumerations.
notes.localization: Enum keys are stored in English. UI display values should be translated based on user locale preferences.
notes.schemaIntegration: D1 schema tables should reference these enumerations via comments (-- ENUM: category.enumName) instead of hardcoded CHECK constraints
